title: KV prefix-hit acceptance harness with semantic-regression tagging
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an acceptance-level harness that exercises prefix/KV cache hits across representative prompt slices and attaches a semantic-regression tag to any output divergence. The goal is to automatically classify whether a cache-hit-related change is a harmless tokenization/formatting delta or a substantive semantic regression that could affect customer-facing outputs. This harness will be used in pre-rollout canaries and CI gating for cache-related config or model changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- The harness runs against configured golden datasets and produces a per-example verdict: identical|format-diff|semantic-regression.
- Semantic-regression verdicts are accompanied by a minimal diff, a semantic-similarity score, and a suggested severity (low/medium/high).
- Harness integrates with canary pipeline to block rollouts when high-severity semantic regressions exceed threshold.
- Results are written to the eval dashboard with hit/non-hit attribution and histogram by model/config variant.
implementation_notes: 1) Use existing golden-response dataset as baseline; extend with synthetic adversarial prefixes for underrepresented motifs (e.g., instruction-following, code blocks, multi-turn context). 2) For semantic comparison, combine lexical diffs with embedding-based cosine similarity (use runtime-approved embedding model) and a small rule-based classifier tuned on historical regressions. 3) Tag cache-hit provenance in request metadata so harness can correlate changes with hit/no-hit. 4) Persist examples with deterministic replay data to S3 for engineering triage.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for diffing/semantic-score logic.
- Shadow canary: run harness in parallel to production traffic for one-week window and compare signal to known incidents.
- Controlled experiments: flip cache gating for 5% of requests and verify harness flags expected divergences.
- Evaluation metrics: true-positive rate vs historical labeled regressions >= 0.85, false-positive rate <= 0.15 for format-only diffs.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — prototype script that replays cached vs uncached responses and computes embedding similarity (Ben Carter).

2026-03-09: Integration PR opened for hit provenance header and replay artifacts; awaiting infra review (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2897).
2026-03-11: Canary pipeline hook implemented; running daily shadow evaluations on canary pool (observability: dashboards/caches/kv-harness-shadows).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: embedding similarity thresholds can be brittle across model upgrades. Mitigation: calibrate per-model baselines and store threshold history, require at least two independent signals (lexical + embedding) before marking semantic-regression. Risk: increased CI runtime. Mitigation: sample-based evaluation and parallelized workers.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on the semantic scoring heuristics and dashboard schema. We need sign-off from Reliability and Product before enabling blocking behavior in canary. If approved, plan to run non-blocking for two full cycles to establish baseline false-positive rate.
